correctness.rationale: The published Das–Mawiong classification provides exactly ten beat-point-free ten-point spaces as seven types and three duals. The three-level incidence matrices determine all homeomorphisms by level-preserving permutations, and the colored omission graph handles Types IV–VII. Independently recomputing all seven finite permutation groups from the actual cover lists yields orders 2,6,4,4,2,2,1 and reverse-order bijection counts 0,0,0,4,0,0,1; element orders distinguish S3 from V4. Dual types preserve their groups. Cianci–Ottina Theorems 3.6–3.7 establish no smaller weakly contractible noncontractible finite space and only the Rival nine-point model and dual at nine; Costoya–Gomes–Viruel §3 explicitly records Aut(Rival)=C2. These cited exhaustive classification theorems, not the seven-model script, justify the universal size threshold. Only beat-point-free uniqueness is asserted at size ten.

final_claim: Ten is the least size of a finite T0 weakly contractible noncontractible space with trivial homeomorphism group. Among the ten classified beat-point-free ten-point cores, only Type VII is rigid; the seven representative automorphism groups are C2,S3,V4,V4,C2,C2,1; Type VII has a unique order-reversing involution.
limitations: Uniqueness only among ten-point beat-point-free spaces; not asserted for all nonminimal size-ten spaces.
